codex.text: Accepting on a single ≥10% expectancy-per-signal delta with no confidence interval, minimum sample size, or significance test means you'd promote noise as readily as edge — and per-signal expectancy is trivially gamed: culling the worst 20% of trades mechanically raises it while total net PnL falls, so aggregate outcome and drawdown/tail behavior must be gated too. Every challenger evaluated against the same sealed holdout burns it through multiple testing; the 10%/20% thresholds must be pre-registered in the registry *before* unsealing, with an explicit budget on holdout reuses, or this is holdout-fitting dressed as governance. The persistence filter also silently shifts entry timing by one bar, changing both the traded population and realized spread/slippage exposure, so "same period and cost assumptions" does not make the comparison apples-to-apples unless entries are re-timestamped and re-costed. Finally, the proposal reads as if the holdout delta alone decides promotion — clarify that all standard `promote.py` gates (walk-forward stability, regime slices, cost-adjusted EV) still apply rather than being bypassed by this bespoke rule.

opencode.text: The “pre-registration” is incomplete: breakeven timing, trailing distance, symbols, regimes, sampling window, cost model, and adaptation rules are unspecified, allowing post-hoc tuning and overfitting to the observed exit labels. A ≥300-trade holdout may still be temporally or instrumentally correlated, and “bootstrap p05 > 0,” “win rate not collapsing below ~55%,” and the expectancy/payoff gates are ambiguous without a predefined test, confidence level, multiplicity control, and power analysis. “Demo-only” and “no live config edits” are asserted rather than technically enforced, so the proposal needs an explicit path-level safety check preventing the challenger from reaching live YAML, order placement, or champion promotion.

proposals.text: **Proposal:** Run one pre-registered demo-only exit experiment targeting the measured payoff asymmetry: realized trades show PF 0.751 with avg_win 0.049 vs avg_loss −0.142 (payoff ratio ~0.34), while tp-exits carry +0.09 expectancy and sl-exits −0.50, and quick_win flattens (1,383) plus never_green flattens (1,288) dominate closes — so replace the quick-win/never-green flatten with a trailing-stop-after-breakeven exit (let winners extend toward TP, keep SL unchanged) as a challenger strategy spec in `bot/research/strategies/`. Falsifiable success gate: on a sealed holdout of ≥300 closed demo round-trips net of runner costs, expectancy must flip from −0.012 to >0 with bootstrap p05 > 0 and payoff ratio ≥0.6 without win rate collapsing below ~55%; if it fails, the challenger is rejected and recorded per the promote gates (`bot/aegis/research/promote.py`). This directly tests the classic "cut losses short, let profits run" prescription (*Technical Analysis of Stock Trends*) and follows the falsification discipline of *Evidence-Based Technical Analysis* (Aronson); no champion change, no live config edits, no order flow outside the existing research/demo sandbox.

Test a two-consecutive-bar persistence requirement for the validated-state gate in a registry-recorded, read-only shadow experiment. Using the same symbols, period, and spread/slippage assumptions, accept it only if the sealed holdout improves net expectancy per signal by at least 10% while reducing signal count by no more than 20%. Otherwise, reject the challenger and leave the champion unchanged.

Accept the challenger only if the pre-specified statistical test supports at least a 10% improvement in net expectancy per signal, while aggregate net PnL is non-inferior or improved, signal count declines no more than 20%, and drawdown and tail-risk metrics remain within pre-registered limits. opencode.text: **Proposal:** Run one pre-registered demo-only exit experiment: on a frozen symbol set (EURUSD, XAUUSD) and regime band (ATR-percentile 20–80) over a fixed sampling window, replace quick-win/never-green flattens with a trailing stop that arms at +0.8R breakeven and trails 1.0×ATR(14) behind the extreme close, SL unchanged — all parameters, window bounds, cost model (runner-recorded spread/slippage per fill), and adaptation rules (any post-hoc change voids the run and is logged as a separate rejected variant) committed to a spec in `bot/research/strategies/` before any holdout is touched. The single primary endpoint, declared ex ante with no multiplicity: net-of-cost expectancy > 0 on ≥300 sealed holdout round-trips, tested at two-sided α=0.05 via a one-day stationary block bootstrap (p05 > 0), jointly requiring payoff ratio ≥ 0.6 and win rate ≥ 55%, with a pre-unsealing power check confirming n≈300 gives ~80% power for Δexpectancy ≈ 0.05 given realized exit variance. Holdout integrity is enforced structurally: chronological split with a ≥30-day embargo gap and per-symbol stratification so temporally/instrumentally correlated trades cannot leak between dev and holdout. "Demo-only" is technically enforced rather than asserted — the experiment runner whitelists writes to `bot/research/strategies/`, `bot/research/sealed_holdouts.jsonl`, and `bot/reports/research/`, asserts against the `PROTECTED_LIVE_YAML` list, uses MT5 strictly read-only, and leaves champion promotion impossible unless every gate in `bot/aegis/research/promote.py` passes plus explicit human approval. Failure flips nothing: the challenger and its full metrics are recorded as rejected via `ExperimentRegistry` and the sealed-holdout log, keeping the falsification discipline of Aronson's *Evidence-Based Technical Analysis* while testing the *Technical Analysis of Stock Trends* "let profits run" prescription.
